beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: You think Buffett sells his big winners? Not this one. Here's why.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Berkshire finished buying these Coca-Cola shares decades ago, for $1.3B in total. Watch what that one purchase does.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Never sold a single share? Then how does he get any money out of it?

actions.name: Dividend
actions.line: A slice of profit, paid in cash

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Coca-Cola pays its owners a slice of its profit every year. That slice is called a dividend.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: When the buying finished, the dividend was $205,479 a day. Worth waiting decades?

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Exactly. Why not sell and buy something faster?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Because Coca-Cola kept raising its dividend, year after year, while Berkshire's cost never moved.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And here's the twist. Decades later, the dividend was $704M a year. That's 54% of the whole price, paid back in one year.

params.header: Keep the tree, eat the fruit

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That's why Berkshire never sold. It keeps the tree and eats the fruit, about $1.9M a day by then.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That's one company's past, not a promise. But would you have kept it all those years, like Buffett?

sources: Data: Berkshire Hathaway 2022 shareholder letter · Dec 2022
